findings.summary: The I2-misnomer deferral is recorded only where the deferee will not look: M4.13f's backlog row and notes say nothing about renaming, so the obligation lives in a test javadoc alone.
findings.failure_scenario: Whoever picks up M4.13f reads its row ('I4's REORDER CLAUSE ... checkReader judges a reader's next-offset map ... needs a per-record consumer trace') and backlog-notes.md, which has no M4.13f section at all. Neither mentions that checkChain labels a permuted-but-disjoint batch 'I2'. M4.13f lands, the reorder clause is closed on the reader side, and the mislabel stays in checkChain permanently -- with a passing test whose assertion description now asserts the mislabel is intended. Fix is one clause on the M4.13f row, not a code change.
